title: Co-Regulation
subtitle: How connection shapes our nervous system

sections.heading: We Are Wired for Connection
sections.content:
Humans are fundamentally social creatures. Our nervous systems evolved to be regulated in relationship with others - this is called co-regulation.

From birth, we learn to regulate our nervous systems through connection with caregivers. Their calm helps us calm. Their presence signals safety. This need for co-regulation continues throughout our lives.

sections.heading: How Co-Regulation Works
sections.content:
When we're with someone whose nervous system is regulated, our own nervous system picks up on cues of safety:

• Their relaxed facial expressions
• Their calm tone of voice
• Their steady breathing
• Their grounded presence

This happens through neuroception - your nervous system reading their nervous system, below conscious awareness.
sections.practicePrompt: Think of someone whose presence naturally calms you. What is it about being with them that helps you feel safe?

sections.heading: Nervous System Contagion
sections.content:
Just as calm can spread between people, so can dysregulation. You've likely experienced:

• Someone's anxiety making you feel anxious
• Walking into a tense room and feeling it
• A crying baby triggering stress in adults

This is why it matters who we spend time with and why regulated communities are healing places.
sections.practicePrompt: Notice who in your life tends to calm your nervous system and who tends to activate it. There's no judgment - just awareness.

sections.heading: Building Co-Regulating Relationships
sections.content:
Not all relationships are co-regulating. Safe, healing relationships include:

• Consistency and reliability
• Attunement to your state
• Respect for boundaries
• Repair after ruptures
• Acceptance of all your states

You deserve relationships where you feel safe to be yourself, even in difficult moments.
sections.practicePrompt: Who are the co-regulating people in your life? How might you nurture those connections this week?

sections.heading: Self-Regulation and Co-Regulation
sections.content:
Self-regulation (calming yourself) and co-regulation (calming with others) work together:

• We develop self-regulation through early co-regulation
• Even as adults, we need both
• It's not weakness to need others
• Strong self-regulation makes us better co-regulators

The goal isn't independence from others, but interdependence - knowing when to reach out and when to go inward.
sections.practicePrompt: Do you tend to over-rely on self-regulation or co-regulation? What would better balance look like?

sections.heading: Offering Co-Regulation to Others
sections.content:
As you develop your own regulation, you become a resource for others. You can offer co-regulation by:

• Staying calm when others are activated
• Listening without trying to fix
• Matching their pace, then gradually slowing
• Staying present through difficult moments
• Modeling taking care of yourself

Your regulated presence is a gift to those around you.
sections.practicePrompt: Think of someone who might benefit from your calm presence. How might you offer co-regulation to them?
